entities.summary: Stanisław Pestkowski was a Polish Bolshevik active in the Russian Revolution of 1917. Born in Kiełczygłów, Poland on December 3, 1882, Pestkowski played a significant role in the Bolshevik movement that sought to overthrow the Russian monarchy. As a key figure in the Russian Revolution, Pestkowski was instrumental in organizing the Bolshevik Party's efforts in the early 20th century. His involvement in the revolution had far-reaching consequences, contributing to the establishment of the Soviet Union and shaping the course of modern Russian history. The legacy of Stanisław Pestkowski continues to be felt in the contemporary Russian political landscape, where his ideas and actions remain a subject of study and debate among scholars and historians. The impact of his life and work can be seen in the numerous books, articles, and documentaries that have explored the Russian Revolution and its aftermath. As a testament to his enduring influence, Pestkowski's name is still invoked by scholars and activists today, who seek to understand the complexities of the Russian Revolution and its ongoing impact on global politics and society.
